diff_size_scale: scopeSize (S ≤50 · M ≤300 · L >300 changed lines) — metrics.mjs, and the value the corpus manifest froze into meta.scope

axes.source: the finding record's own `severity`, after the arm boundary translated CodeRabbit's `trivial` to `nit`
axes.note: CodeRabbit's largest tier is `trivial`, which is not on our scale; `adapters/coderabbit.mjs` translates it and this axis reads the translated value. Re-translating here would apply the translation twice
FIVE classes, which is what `FILE_CLASSES` holds. §4's six (frontend/backend/docs/config/tests/harness) never existed in the code it cited

axes.scale: scopeSize (S ≤50 · M ≤300 · L >300 changed lines) — metrics.mjs, and the value the corpus manifest froze into meta.scope
axes.source: `scopeSize(meta.additions, meta.deletions)`, cross-checked against the `meta.scope` the manifest froze beside them
axes.note: the OTHER scale §4 names — five buckets, XS…XL — is implemented nowhere in scripts/, so it is not offered here rather than being invented

measured: only 3 autonomous pull requests exist in the 106-PR candidate pool, so a difference along this axis cannot be ATTRIBUTED to authorship even where n clears the threshold. The cells are reported; the attribution is not available

axes.source: the origin the replay's own novelty gate FROZE onto the record (`panel.novelty.origin`)
axes.note: read off the record, never recomputed: `noveltyOf` is async and reads git, so a scorer calling it would answer a question about today's tree instead of the reviewed one. CodeRabbit records have no counterpart, so this axis is one-armed

THEIR taxonomy, not ours, and it is discovered from the data rather than declared because we do not own it. Never a defect-type axis: it is a pre-run proxy for one, and conflating the two would report their routing as our ground truth

axes.source: `coderabbit.window` — which snapshot of the pull request the finding is about
axes.note: not an insight axis but a comparability one, and it is here because `assertComparableWindow` names this scorer as the remedy: a finding about code our arm never reviewed may be SEGMENTED but never pooled. Our arm has no window field, so it is one-armed by construction rather than by choice

axes.reason: defect type is assigned at adjudication and no adjudicated labels exist, so there is nothing to cut by. Pre-filling it from a lens id would report our own routing as a property of the defect

metrics.spec: §3.1 — share of findings that are `nit` or `minor`
§3.1 — share of findings citing a file and line that resolves against the frozen diff
§3.1 — scope discipline: share of findings anchored inside a changed region
§3.1 — findings per 100 diff lines, which is severely size-confounded and must be read per size bucket rather than pooled

pairs_not_computed.reason: the nit ratio is a function of severity, so `severity=nit` reports 1.000 and `severity=major` reports 0.000 by construction
findings_per_pr is counted in PRs and severity cuts findings, so every bucket would share one denominator — that is a numerator filter, not a segment (§4.1)
findings_per_100_lines is counted in PRs with a known diff size and severity cuts findings, so every bucket would share one denominator — that is a numerator filter, not a segment (§4.1)
findings_per_pr is counted in PRs and file_class cuts findings, so every bucket would share one denominator — that is a numerator filter, not a segment (§4.1)
findings_per_100_lines is counted in PRs with a known diff size and file_class cuts findings, so every bucket would share one denominator — that is a numerator filter, not a segment (§4.1)

the novelty annotation is stamped ONLY on critical/major findings (`annotateFindings` returns non-blockers untouched), so every annotated bucket has a nit ratio of 0 and `not-annotated` has 1 — measured 0.000 · 0.000 · 1.000 on the pilot. The novelty axis is severity-confounded by construction, which is a fact about the annotation and not about the code's age
findings_per_pr is counted in PRs and novelty cuts findings, so every bucket would share one denominator — that is a numerator filter, not a segment (§4.1)
findings_per_100_lines is counted in PRs with a known diff size and novelty cuts findings, so every bucket would share one denominator — that is a numerator filter, not a segment (§4.1)
findings_per_pr is counted in PRs and coderabbit_category cuts findings, so every bucket would share one denominator — that is a numerator filter, not a segment (§4.1)
findings_per_100_lines is counted in PRs with a known diff size and coderabbit_category cuts findings, so every bucket would share one denominator — that is a numerator filter, not a segment (§4.1)
findings_per_pr is counted in PRs and window cuts findings, so every bucket would share one denominator — that is a numerator filter, not a segment (§4.1)
findings_per_100_lines is counted in PRs with a known diff size and window cuts findings, so every bucket would share one denominator — that is a numerator filter, not a segment (§4.1)

census.reason: novelty has no counterpart in the coderabbit arm — the origin the replay's own novelty gate FROZE onto the record (`panel.novelty.origin`)
coderabbit_category has no counterpart in the panel arm — `coderabbit.category` — CodeRabbit's own CHILL vocabulary, verbatim
window has no counterpart in the panel arm — `coderabbit.window` — which snapshot of the pull request the finding is about
